## b5c38cb14599

**Concrete shortcut:** the operation key is sampled independently rather than
scheduled across a four-demonstration lesson. With seed `5` and sample indices
`0,1,2,3,4`, the generated top-left keys are exactly
`[1, 3, 3, 3, 2]`. Thus the four demonstrations contain union once and xor
three times, while the query asks for intersection without any demonstration
of key `2`.

A solver can fit every demonstration while leaving key `2` undefined or
mapping it to a default operation. This is especially risky because randomly
constructed normalized shapes can also make union and xor observationally
similar when their masks do not overlap. Schedule keys `1`, `2`, and `3` into
every lesson and include mask pairs whose overlaps make all three operations
produce distinct outputs. No source change was made as part of this audit.
